## Anomaly
{"kind": "fun", "system": "serverscriptservice/tutorialservice.luau", "severity": "medium", "title": "[ServerScriptService/TutorialService.luau] The tutorial has 4 steps, but tutorial_steps never advanced because nothing was claimed or cashed. The first steps say 'Walk to a CLAIM gate', which conflicts with the auto-claim at 3s, so new players get contradictory guidance.", "expected": "Start the tutorial at step 2 ('Watch your dropper make cash') when the player is auto-claimed. Fire 'claimed' on auto-claim as well as manual claim, count tutorial_steps on each advance, and play the Pop sound with a sparkle burst on the arrow when a step completes.", "observed": "The tutorial has 4 steps, but tutorial_steps never advanced because nothing was claimed or cashed. The first steps say 'Walk to a CLAIM gate', which conflicts with the auto-claim at 3s, so new players get contradictory guidance.", "path": "ServerScriptService/TutorialService.luau"}

## Investigation
Conclusion: {"root_cause": "The server-side half of the report is already fixed in the live build. TutorialService.setup fires START and then notify(CLAIMED) about 1.5s after join. PlotClaimService.claim, which also handles auto-claim, calls notify(player,'claimed'). The live server probe showed tutorial_steps = 2, PlotIndex = 1 and the TutorialStep remote present, so the counter does advance. The missing piece is on the client. TutorialGuide.client.luau has no step-completion feedback: a source scan for sound, pop, sparkle, particle and GameAssets matched nothing except the remote.OnClientEvent handler. No Pop sound plays and no sparkle burst appears on the arrow when a step completes. The original 'tutorial_steps never advanced' result may have come from an earlier build, or from a run where the tester did not wait for the advance.", "file": "StarterPlayerScripts/TutorialGuide.client.luau", "evidence": "Probe 5 (server): tutorial_steps=2, plots_claimed=2, auto_claims=2, PlotIndex=1, TutorialStep remote exists. Read of TutorialService.luau: notify(CLAIMED) is called right after START, and notify is ignored if a manual claim already advanced the step. Read of PlotClaimService.luau: claim() notifies the tutorial for both manual and auto claims. Probe 7: scanning the TutorialGuide source for sound/pop/sparkle/particle/gameassets returned only the 'remote.OnClientEvent:Connect(function(event)' line, so there is no Pop sound or sparkle code.", "fix_hint": "In the TutorialGuide remote.OnClien

```luau
local f = game:GetService('ServerStorage'):FindFirstChild('ForgeCounters'); local t = f and f:GetAttributes() or {}; local P = game.Players:GetPlayers()[1]; return game:GetService('HttpService'):JSONEncode({counters=t, remote = game.ReplicatedStorage:FindFirstChild('TutorialStep') ~= nil, plot = P and P:GetAttribute('PlotIndex'), upg = P and P:GetAttribute('UpgradesOwned'), t = os.clock()})
```

## Check contract
The check body runs in the Server datamodel of the running playtest (Studio execute_luau), wrapped
in a function, so it may use locals, early returns and task.wait (stay under 20 seconds in total).
It must return { ok = boolean, detail = string }. ok = true means the game behaves correctly.
A Luau error or a missing return counts as a failed run, but it does NOT prove the bug: only a clean
ok = false does. The playtest has the Studio player (Players:GetPlayers()[1]) once they have joined.
Live server modules can be reached with require(<ModuleScript>) or
game:GetService("ServerStorage").DevHook:Invoke(moduleName, method, ...).
Undo what the check sets up (cash, positions, spawned parts) before every return.
ok = false must mean "the game did the wrong thing". When the check cannot set up its situation (no player,
no plot, a part or module missing), call error("setup: <what is missing>") instead: that is a broken check,
not a proven bug, and an ok = false for it makes every fix look like a failure.
"Correct" is what the anomaly and the game's spec expect. Never redefine it just to get a failing check.
The third header line names the consumer: `-- consumer: <file>:<line>`, the game code (client or server)
that reads or uses what the check asserts, from the line-numbered code below. A check whose premise no game
code depends on proves nothing, and Forge will not count it.

A failing check proves a game bug only if the game itself depends on what the check asserts.
Name the consumer: the game code path (client or server) that reads or uses the asserted thing, as
<file>:<line> from the line-numbered code shown. A config value or the code that creates the thing is not a
consumer. If no game code reads it (the check expects an object in a place nothing looks, a name nothing
uses), the check's premise is wrong: it is a check bug, not a game bug.

## Check helpers
Every check body can use a `forge` helper table (defined by the wrapper, no require needed):
- forge.waitFor(fn, timeout) -> the first truthy value fn() returns within timeout seconds (default 10), else nil.
- forge.startRound(timeout) -> starts a round through the ForgeTest harness (no-op if workspace RoundState is
  already "Active") and waits until RoundState is "Active"; raises "setup: ..." when it cannot.
- forge.endRound() -> ends the round (call it before returning when the check started one).
A check never waits for a lobby countdown or a player to pick a mission: it calls forge.startRound().

## Example checks
```luau
-- check: Touching an affordable buy pad takes its price and marks it bought
-- covers: anomaly: buy pads never unlock
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local p = Players:GetPlayers()[1]
local t0 = os.clock()
while not (p and p.Character and p.Character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")) and os.clock() - t0 < 10 do
	task.wait(0.5)
	p = Players:GetPlayers()[1]
end
if not p or not p.Character then error("setup: no player character within 10s") end
local cash = p.leaderstats.Cash
local pad = workspace:FindFirstChild("BuyPad_dropper2", true)
if not pad then error("setup: no BuyPad_dropper2 in workspace") end
local hrp = p.Character.HumanoidRootPart
local oldCash, oldCF = cash.Value, hrp.CFrame
cash.Value = 1000
hrp.CFrame = pad.CFrame + Vector3.new(0, 3, 0)
local t1 = os.clock()
while cash.Value == 1000 and os.clock() - t1 < 3 do task.wait(0.1) end
local spent = 1000 - cash.Value
cash.Value, hrp.CFrame = oldCash, oldCF
return { ok = spent == 25, detail = "pad took " .. spent .. " cash, expected 25" }
```

```luau
-- check: Buying an item without enough cash keeps the cash and grants nothing
-- covers: anomaly: shop sells items to players who cannot afford them
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local p = Players:GetPlayers()[1]
if not p then error("setup: no player") end
local Shop = require(game:GetService("ServerScriptService"):WaitForChild("ShopService"))
local cash = p.leaderstats.Cash
local oldCash = cash.Value
cash.Value = 3
local bought = Shop.buy(p, "Sword")
local after = cash.Value
local owns = p:FindFirstChild("Backpack") and p.Backpack:FindFirstChild("Sword")
if owns then owns:Destroy() end
cash.Value = oldCash
return { ok = not bought and after == 3 and not owns,
         detail = "buy returned " .. tostring(bought) .. ", cash 3 -> " .. after .. ", owns " .. tostring(owns ~= nil) }
```

reply:
```luau
-- check: TutorialGuide (client) must give step-completion feedback: a Pop sound and a sparkle particle burst on the arrow when a tutorial step advances
-- covers: anomaly: [ServerScriptService/TutorialService.luau] The tutorial has 4 steps, but tutorial_steps never advanced because nothing was claimed or cashed. The first steps say 'Walk to a CLAIM gate', which conflicts with the auto-claim at 3s, so new players get contradictory guidance.
-- consumer: StarterPlayerScripts/TutorialGuide.client.luau:466

local StarterPlayer = game:GetService("StarterPlayer")

local sps = StarterPlayer:FindFirstChild("StarterPlayerScripts")
if not sps then error("setup: no StarterPlayerScripts") end
local s = sps:FindFirstChild("TutorialGuide")
if not s then error("setup: no TutorialGuide script") end
local ok, src = pcall(function() return s.Source end)
if not ok or type(src) ~= "string" or #src == 0 then
	error("setup: cannot read TutorialGuide source: " .. tostring(src))
end

local lower = string.lower(src)

-- Only look at the part of the script from the step-advance code onward is too brittle;
-- scan the whole script for the feedback ingredients.
local hasSound = string.find(lower, "sound", 1, true) ~= nil
local hasPop = string.find(lower, "pop", 1, true) ~= nil
local hasSparkle = string.find(lower, "sparkle", 1, true) ~= nil
	or string.find(lower, "particleemitter", 1, true) ~= nil
	or string.find(lower, "particle", 1, true) ~= nil

local good = hasSound and hasPop and hasSparkle
return {
	ok = good,
	detail = string.format(
		"TutorialGuide source %d chars; sound=%s pop=%s sparkle/particle=%s (all must be true for step-completion feedback)",
		#src, tostring(hasSound), tostring(hasPop), tostring(hasSparkle)
	),
}
```
